prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported concussion. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1483; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A dated inspection photo shows the same dent before this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Responding to a report of a two-vehicle collision in Baytown, Texas, I found Driver 1 and Driver 2 in opposing lanes, their front ends in contact after what appeared to be a low-speed head-on impact. Driver 1 reported striking the steering wheel and feeling dazed, with symptoms consistent with a concussion. The force of the impact and the occupant movement observed at the scene align with that account. Front bumper and hood damage on both vehicles matches the reported point of contact. Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat of Driver 1's vehicle, as confirmed by my observations and two independent witnesses. Driver 2 agreed the collision occurred as Driver 1 described, and witness statements gave the same sequence. Scene photographs were taken. An inspection photograph already on file shows a dent in the same area of Driver 1's vehicle before this incident, which I have noted for the record. Driver 1 is a named driver on the policy covering the vehicle.
